title: DDB flushes subnormal factor/life before multiplying by cost and uses a u32::MAX integer-power threshold
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20430, DDB(cost, salvage, life, period, [factor]) evaluates rate = RN53(RN64(factor / life)) and flushes a subnormal rate to 0 before multiplying by cost, evaluates (1 - rate)^(period - 1) via an x87-stored binary-squaring loop when period - 1 is an integer below u32::MAX (and via excel_pow_positive at or above u32::MAX), and checks declining-amount overflow before clipping to salvage. All 1,761 full-bank DDB rows match.
basis: Measured in CalcFunc-Evidence cache/w111-depreciation-20260929/answers-ddb.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and Excel 16.0.20527.20088 (f3_financial row 9); 1,761/1,761 full-bank rows match.
inferred: That the internal u32::MAX boundary and x87-stored staging apply identically across arbitrary untested extreme-period inputs beyond the 1,761 full-bank rows is inferred.
